title.title: Assignment: Your First Transaction
title.subtitle: The hands-on finale. Send one real transaction on a testnet: it stores the hash of your student number in the Academy's smart contract. Then find it on Etherscan.

brief.heading: One transaction, three steps
brief.subtitle: Send one transaction to the Academy's smart contract: it stores the hash of your student number. That is the whole assignment, and the wizard on the next slide guides every click.

steps.title: Set up
steps.lead: Get a [wallet](kw:wallet) on the Sepolia testnet, with a few free test coins in it.
items: Install a wallet: Rabby, Zerion or MetaMask. Use a fresh one, with no real funds.
Get free test ETH from a Sepolia faucet. It pays for gas and has no real value.
Connect the wallet to the wizard and switch it to Sepolia.
steps.result: a wallet on Sepolia holding test ETH.

steps.title: Register
steps.lead: Send one [transaction](kw:transaction) that stores the [hash](kw:hash) of your student number in the Academy's contract.
items: Type your student number into the wizard.
It is hashed in your browser with keccak256, the hash function Ethereum uses. Only the hash is sent.
Press Send transaction and confirm in your wallet: you sign, and you pay the gas.
steps.result: a confirmed transaction, and your hash stored next to your address.

steps.title: Verify
steps.lead: Find your transaction on Etherscan, and the value it left in the contract's [state](kw:state).
items: The wizard shows your transaction hash and a link to Etherscan.
Open the link: your address under From, the Academy's contract under To, status Success.
Back in the wizard, check the stored value: read from the contract, it matches your hash.
steps.result: your transaction hash and its Etherscan link. Keep them: they are your proof.

brief.optional: Optional, afterwards: explore a real contract
notes: The contract is deployed by the Academy on Sepolia. Its address is wired into the wizard and will be shared in class.
Public and permanent. Only the hash goes on-chain, yet anyone who already knows your student number can compute the same hash.
Testnet only: never real funds, and never type a recovery phrase into a website.

board.heading: Registered hashes
board.subtitle: Every wallet that has registered and the hash it holds now, read live from the contract. Type a student number to check that its hash is on the list, and which wallet put it there.

explore.badge: Optional · not part of the assignment
explore.heading: Explore a real contract
explore.subtitle: Done with your transaction and curious? Read contracts that hold real money, then poke a tiny one on the testnet. Nothing here is required.

usdc.look: A proxy: Code opens the logic contract. Find blacklist and pause. Who is allowed to call them?

weth.look: Short, with no owner and no admin. Find deposit and withdraw. Who could change these rules?

dai.look: Find mint, then the word auth next to it. Which addresses does that let through?

explore.questionsLabel: Talk it through: four questions for any contract

questions.label: State
questions.desc: What does it remember? Find where the balances live.

questions.label: Functions
questions.desc: Which actions does it offer? Which only read, and which change state and cost gas?

questions.label: Access
questions.desc: Which functions can anyone call, and which need a special role?

questions.label: Limits
questions.desc: Who, if anyone, can still change the rules after deployment?

poke.label: Poke · anyone can write to this one
poke.what: a greeting and a counter, in under 30 lines
steps: Read Contract: note greeting and counter.
Write Contract: press Connect to Web3 (wallet on Sepolia), type a greeting into setGreeting, confirm.
Read again: the greeting is yours and counter went up by one. Until someone overwrites it.
poke.warning: Public and permanent: write nothing personal. This contract is not ours, and anyone can overwrite the greeting.

keyPoints.s8-first-tx: Submit your hashed student ID and the transaction link on Moodle for Assignment 2.
keyPoints.s8-board: Reading a contract's state is free and open to everyone. Only writing to it takes a signature and gas.
keyPoints.s8-explore: Verified source means you don't have to take a contract's word for it: read the code, then check the state yourself.
